PullRequest.Title: Revamp tabbed model picker UI card
PullRequest.Body: Adjust the tabbed model picker UI card to now use icons and a separate entry point for faster thinking level configuration

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new listener, synchronous emitter, card `finally` render, and changed completion callback establish three card rebuilds without timing assumptions.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM nodes, controls, managed hovers, rendered descriptions, and allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Three full rebuilds per successful option choice; each grows with option, warning, action, description, and pricing content.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher input latency plus CPU and GC pressure from repeated synchronous DOM reconstruction.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The card rebuilt once in `_setValues`; `onDidAccept` refreshed only the backing list, and no scoped listener independently refreshed the card.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: One option save now invokes picker refresh from the synchronous scoped-change event, the card's existing completion render, and another picker refresh from `onDidAccept`.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 575 changes `onDidAccept` from refreshing only the backing list to `this.refresh()`, which refreshes the mounted details card even though `ModelCard._setValues` has just rebuilt it; added line 159 also refreshes it from the same save's scoped-change event.
Findings.Title: Coalesce configuration-driven card refreshes
Findings.Impact: Choosing effort or context can jank because the mounted details subtree is reconstructed three times for one click.
Findings.Evidence: `ChatModelConfigurationStore._applyLocalModelConfiguration` synchronously fires `onDidChange` before persistence finishes. The new listener calls `TabbedModelPicker.refresh`, which calls `_getModelCard(...).refresh()`. `ModelCard._setValues` then calls `_renderPreservingFocus` in `finally` and invokes `onDidAccept`; line 575 calls `refresh()` and rebuilds the card again. `_render` clears and recreates radios, actions, hovers, description content, banners, and pricing rows.
Findings.Recommendation: Coalesce internal save notifications into one card rebuild; keep external-change refreshes, but make `onDidAccept` update only list/footer summaries or deduplicate the listener and completion refresh.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Constructor rendering, the unconditional refresh, and the render method's full clear/recreate behavior are directly visible; only the exact milliseconds vary with card content.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM nodes, Radio and ActionBar controls, hover objects, rendered description nodes, and pricing rows
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Paid once per distinct model inspected during each popup lifetime; each duplicate render grows with the model's options, messages, actions, description, and pricing metrics.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased details-opening latency and avoidable CPU/GC pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A newly created hover details card rendered once in its constructor and was mounted directly.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The first details opening for each inspected model constructs the complete card subtree and then immediately clears and reconstructs it before mounting the page.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 605 unconditionally calls `card.refresh()` immediately after `_getModelCard`; for an uncached model, `_getModelCard` has just run `new ModelCard(cardOptions)`, whose constructor already calls `_render()`.
Findings.Title: Skip the second render of a newly created details card
Findings.Impact: The first click into a model's details performs twice the necessary synchronous DOM/control construction, delaying page display and creating avoidable allocation/GC pressure.
Findings.Evidence: `ModelCard`'s constructor invokes `_render()`. `_showModelDetails` obtains that new card and immediately invokes `refresh()`, which calls `_renderPreservingFocus()` and `_render()` again. `_render()` clears both card and header and recreates radio controls, action bars, managed hover, rendered description, warnings/promotions, and pricing rows. The former hover-card creation path returned a newly constructed card without this second render.
Findings.Recommendation: Refresh only reused cached cards. Have `_getModelCard` report whether it created the card, or move the freshness check into that method so a just-constructed card is not rendered again.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the tabbed model picker, browse provider tabs/search results, and open model details
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Destination/section construction, model-row rendering, then details-card construction and popup layout are synchronous on the click path. No subprocess, IPC, database, or network operation must complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Available models and visible rows control list work; details work scales with one inspected model's configuration options, messages, actions, description, and pricing rows. List virtualization bounds mounted row toolbars, while first details entry is one card at a time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread render path; no parallel boundary work. Toolbar focus updates scan only mounted toolbars.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Scoped model configurations become in-memory after first access. Model cards are cached per model for the popup lifetime and disposed on hide; the PR nevertheless renders a newly created card twice before first mount, which was reported.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed row/card construction, caching, layout reads, and widget lifecycle were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact first-open delay varies with model metadata and browser layout cost; the duplicate full render is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity repeated rendering on first details entry; other list and layout work is bounded and local.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose thinking effort, context, Auto tier, or reset configuration from the details page
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected value is applied locally, persisted through model configuration services, then the card and list summaries are refreshed. Successful persistence is awaited before the card's completion path finishes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist scoped configuration to storage and update the language-model provider configuration/settings group
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scoped storage update and at most one provider-group settings update per real option change; no-op re-selections skip the global write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configuration persistence occurred, followed by one card rebuild and a list-only refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The save is awaited before completion rendering and model selection. The PR does not increase write cardinality, but adds repeated synchronous card rebuilds before/after this boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected model and one configuration choice per activation; DOM rebuild cost grows with that card's controls, messages, rendered description, actions, and pricing rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `ModelCard` serializes activations and the PR adds `SequencerByKey` serialization per model; different model keys could run concurrently, but the UI exposes one details card, so realistic interaction is one active key.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration values and schemas are read from the scoped store/in-memory model service after initialization. The scoped change event is synchronous for local updates; no negative-cache behavior is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: synchronous event emission, awaited persistence, existing card render, and both added picker refreshes were traced end to end.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Persistence and DOM duration vary by host and card complexity, but three card rebuilds per successful choice are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity repeated UI reconstruction; persisted boundary cardinality and per-key serialization remain bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Receive model-catalogue, scoped-configuration, pin, trust, or picker-setting changes while the popup is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Events synchronously refresh or hide the popup; model changes rebuild destinations/sections and the active list. Refreshes while details are visible are coalesced into one pending list refresh on Back.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Available model count, provider destinations, and the number of emitted configuration events. Effective list work is collection-wide per event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event handlers run serially on the UI thread. Details-mode list refresh uses a boolean pending flag, preventing repeated hidden-list rebuilds until return.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Speed-variant maps are cleared only when model inputs change; cards live for one popup and are disposed on hide. Configuration reads are cached by the scoped store after first access.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for refresh scheduling and lifecycle; no transitive external operation is invoked by the refresh itself.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalogue and conversation-change event frequency varies, but no additional high-confidence boundary fan-out or unbounded retention was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression: refreshes are event-driven, hidden-list work is coalesced, and popup/card resources have explicit cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll, resize, and keyboard-navigate the details page and row action toolbars
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Scroll events update the custom scrollbar; resize observers request context-view layout; focus changes update focusability of mounted row toolbars. All work is local synchronous DOM/UI work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scroll/resize frequency and mounted visible row count; virtualization bounds toolbar count, and the details page contains one card.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser events are processed serially on the UI thread; no async fan-out or external boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache lookup is involved; observers/listeners belong to the details disposable store and are removed on Back or popup disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listeners, observers, mounted collection ownership, and disposal were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser-specific layout cost varies, but no forced-layout loop or unbounded per-frame collection was proven.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression beyond the submitted duplicate render findings; event work is bounded and cleanup is explicit.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review across all changed files. Submitted two repeated-render findings: three details-card rebuilds per configuration choice and a redundant second render on first details entry. Traced UI critical paths, configuration persistence, caching, concurrency, event coalescing, and lifecycle cleanup; no additional boundary fan-out, unbounded retention, or high-confidence synchronous layout regression was found.
